report.summary: Cause: in `ship()` in `public/src/store.js`, the confirmed order was merged into the existing order object with `Object.assign`, and then the same `orders` array was passed to `set()`. `set()` skips the update when nothing it was given has changed identity, so subscribers never heard about the change and the view never re-rendered. The server had changed the order, which is why a reload showed "Shipped". Fix: after the server confirms, `ship()` now builds a new `orders` array with a replaced order object, so the view re-renders and shows "Shipped" with no button. The failure path is unchanged: the row keeps its status and "Could not update the order." is shown. I added two tests to `test/store.test.js`, one for a successful ship and one for a failed update.
report.verification: `npm test` passes, 6 of 6 tests, including the two new ones. I also drove the real page with Playwright against a server I started and then stopped by its PID. I opened Orders, selected Packed and clicked Mark shipped on ORD-1002. The row changed to "Shipped" and the button disappeared, with no reload. I did not use the Recovery Probe checks or `compare_reports`, so there is no probe before-and-after comparison. I did not record a before-change baseline for the original bug either.
